items.content_html:
Description of changes

  • replace 'includeBuildDependencies' with explicit list of dependencies from nixos/tests/installer.nix to reduce size of vm disk image
  • add log for output from '--install-bootloader' command

Reduces nixos-disk-image (vm disk image) size to something hydra can build.
Dependencies list was copied from nixos/tests/installer.nix:
https://www.github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/6c31eb9b990446880000e3297f69f4fdee5b69d7/nixos/tests/installer.nix#L612-L642

Size for nixosTests.nixos-rebuild-install-bootloader before change:

/nix/store/7i3fqch8br2dnpnf9kxw6y9w3g8646wn-nixos-disk-image                             32.0G

Fixes build failure of nixosTests.nixos-rebuild-install-bootloader on hydra with "Output limit exceeded" (never built successfully of hydra):
https://hydra.nixos.org/job/nixos/trunk-combined/nixos.tests.nixos-rebuild-install-bootloader.x86_64-linux
https://hydra.nixos.org/build/270105347

For future ref, there may be a way to do it without building nixos-disk-image at all.
But if you set virtualisation.useBootLoader = false; there is no partition table in /dev/vdb and grub while doing --install-loader warns about it which may not be desirable for test purposes (thought test still passes):

There may also be some way to not create disk image, but still use bootloader with some combination of useBootLoader,mountHostNixStore, additionalPaths and useDefaultFilesystems (or doing manual partitioning/bootloader install), but I have not figured it out.
This seems to be the part where disk image is created:
https://www.github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/6c31eb9b990446880000e3297f69f4fdee5b69d7/nixos/modules/virtualisation/qemu-vm.nix#L111-L121

items.content_html:
Description of changes

Building a NixOS disk image results in an error when compiled without Nix tooling, as indicated by the use of the option nix.enable = false;. Disabling Nix tools through this option not only deactivates general Nix tools but also deletes NixOS installer tools. Consequently, an error is encountered in the nixos/lib/make-disk-image.nix file due to the absence of the nixos-install component.

To address this issue, it is worth noting the availability of the system.disableInstallerTools option, which serves the purpose of disabling installer tools specifically. Therefore, adjusting the configuration by using nix.enable = false; should not interfere with the presence of NixOS installation tools, as this can be managed separately through system.disableInstallerTools.

Component:

nixos/installer/tools: remove nix tooling dependency from nixos config

items.content_html:
Description of changes

With 23.11, nixos-containers won't build unless the option nixpkgs.hostPlatform is set.

Here's a minimal reproducible example:

{
  description = "nixos-containers bug demo";

  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/23.11";

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs }: {
    nixosModules.default = { pkgs, modulesPath, ... }: {
      containers.foo.config = {
        environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.hello ];
        system.stateVersion = "22.05";
      };
      system.stateVersion = "22.05";
    };

    nixosConfigurations = {
      broken = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem rec {
        pkgs = nixpkgs.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux;
        modules = [
          "${nixpkgs}/nixos/modules/virtualisation/qemu-vm.nix"
          self.nixosModules.default
        ];
      };
    };
  };
}

This results in the following error:

❯ nix flake check
error: Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set.
       You can set nixpkgs.hostPlatform in hardware-configuration.nix by re-running
       a recent version of nixos-generate-config.
       The option nixpkgs.system is still fully supported for NixOS 22.05 interoperability,
       but will be deprecated in the future, so we recommend to set nixpkgs.hostPlatform.

This PR fixes the problem by using pkgs.stdenv instead of nixpkgs.system.

efingerd is another finger daemon, giving you complete control over what are you going to display about your computer. It's similar to bsd-fingerd, however efingerd allows the user complete control over what to send via .efingerd executable in their home directory. efingerd also has the ability to use the ident protocol to allow the user to configure a different responses per the querier's username and host.

items.content_html:
Ente.io is an application to host an end-to-end encrypted platform for photos and videos. This PR adds a NixOS module to host the ente stack, a nixos test and a documentation page. The module consists of the API server (museum) and several SPA web frontends (nginx). These can be hosted independently of one another.

Specifically this will host:

  • photos (the main app)
  • accounts (passkeys)
  • albums (shared albums)
  • cast (TV casting)

This does not host:

  • billing / payments
  • families (family plan management)

Description of changes

NOTE: This PR is a successor of #398457.
Scope change: The package has been merged in #398489! 🎉

Original description:

Draupnir is a hardfork of Mjolnir. Mjolnir package has been unmaintained due to upstream bugs. This package is mostly a drop-in replacement. This package also uses newer methods of handling dependencies.

Repository can be found at:
https://github.com/the-draupnir-project/Draupnir

Note on testing: package and module were (and still are) tested in our production environment, works fine as far as it's been used.
Note on replacing Mjolnir: Not sure whether this is appropriate, due to general usage of the bot changing. You can however fully automatically migrate from mjolnir to draupnir.
